title: Authoritative clause universe is not yet accessible
analysis: Repository cross-references cannot establish that every requirement, table and annex is covered. User confirms licensed 2018 source exists; the supplied Windows search link is not accessible from this cloud machine.
action: Obtain all 12 parts; build a verified requirement-level inventory with page provenance, normative/informative classification and ASIL applicability.
closure: Source verified, all inventory entries counted, and independent coverage reconciliation completed.

title: The current staffing decision blocks the planned governance gate
analysis: The safety plan explicitly says the no-assessor decision prevents G0 under its existing CR-01/CR-03 plan. AI review cannot silently satisfy that requirement.
action: Reconcile staffing decision and confirmation plan; appoint qualified reviewers and assessor or formally re-plan without claiming gate completion.
closure: Named roles, competence/conflict declarations, approved plan and signed confirmation records.

title: AI-generated review has no independent verification credit under the project rules
analysis: This workbook is an assessment aid. The project explicitly assigns AI audits I0; this deliverable cannot be counted as an I1/I3 confirmation or signed FSA.
action: Arrange human review appropriate to the approved ASIL and maintain a separate evidence acceptance trail.
closure: Qualified reviewer signs baseline-specific findings and disposition; independence is evidenced.

title: Safety integrity ratings depend on unverified OEM/driver assumptions
analysis: The HARA explicitly increases the steering case from C to D if credited EPS assumptions are not verified. Current lower targets cannot be treated as established.
action: Verify assumptions per exact ECU/configuration; challenge S/E/C rationale and document both credited and failed-assumption variants.
closure: Approved HARA, witnessed characterization records, configuration binding and independent confirmation.

title: Reduced-authority strategy is a recommendation rather than an approved safety basis
analysis: Option (c) requires measured controllability and speed-dependent limits before re-rating; ASIL reduction and decomposition are different arguments.
action: Record the strategy decision, validate limits and re-rate only after justified controllability; preserve original integrity demands until then.
closure: Signed strategy plus validated limit data, revised allocations and confirmed HARA.

title: Assessment configuration is not fully identified
analysis: VIN, ECU firmware, device revision and harness identity are still open items. A generation-level vehicle label is insufficient to bind physical evidence.
action: Freeze an assessed configuration including hardware serial/revision, ECU firmware, software/submodules, models and calibration.
closure: Complete configuration record and matching manifests for every cited result.

title: Part-specific hardware metrics are not demonstrated
analysis: WP-H-04 lacks BOM-based calculation; WP-H-03 has generic estimates, not part-specific compliance evidence. Generic results cannot close the metric obligation.
action: Acquire BOM/mission profile/failure-rate evidence, validate fault classes and diagnostic coverage, compute per-goal metrics and sensitivity.
closure: Reviewed FMEDA and reproducible part-specific SPFM/LFM/PMHF with traceable inputs and valid targets.

title: Generic FMEDA values must remain separated from demonstrated metrics
analysis: Generic SG-01 SPFM 96.9% and SG-07 86.8% miss the document targets; improved planned-measure values assume implementation and coverage. These are planning warnings, not verified pass/fail results.
action: Label estimates, planned architecture and measured results separately; reconcile WP-H-03 with WP-H-04/05 and confirm target authority.
closure: One configuration-consistent calculation set; planned mechanisms excluded until coverage is substantiated.

title: Documented warning latency exceeds the stated warning budget
analysis: The document records up to 1.26 s against SG-02 1 s; starting the clock after 1 s persistence can conceal end-to-end delay. This is a documented requirement discrepancy, not a new hardware measurement.
action: Resolve the requirement/detection-time definition and measure fault onset through actuation removal and audible warning under worst-case load.
closure: Approved consistent timing budget and witnessed end-to-end traces including tolerance and jitter.

title: Curve-bound time to departure is shorter than assumed driver reaction
analysis: The repository estimates roughly 0.7 s at the ODD bound and itself requests a controllability re-rating or tighter ODD. Driver supervision is not an automatic mitigation.
action: Validate dynamics at the boundary; revise ODD, authority or hazard controllability and flow changes through FSC/TSRs.
closure: Measured validated model, updated ODD and accepted HARA/FTTI rationale.

title: Stock PCS forwarding-loss budget has zero timing margin
analysis: The stated sum of detection and reaction equals FTTI before measured PCS timing. A watchdog nominal setting is insufficient to prove the end-to-end budget.
action: Measure forwarding-loss response and PCS effects; include oscillator tolerance, scheduling, bus delay and safe-state behavior.
closure: Worst-case FDTI+FRTI substantiated with positive justified margin or an explicitly accepted alternative safety argument.

title: Freedom from interference is not established
analysis: The current verdicts include not shown and partially shown; the envelope-only ASIL allocation depends on resolving spatial, timing, communication and boot interference.
action: Reconcile analysis to current pins, bound QM-triggered paths, document separation properties and verify adverse inputs and boot integrity.
closure: Reviewed FFI/DFA with traceable evidence for every interference channel and justified ASIL allocation.

title: The controlled Part 6 lifecycle has not been activated
analysis: The specification explicitly says entry prerequisites are draft/unapproved and Part 6 stays deferred. Existing code and host tests do not establish lifecycle completion.
action: Close E-01…E-15 prerequisites and record the authorized lifecycle baseline and activation decision.
closure: Approved entry checklist, input baselines, confirmation records and activation decision.

title: HIL deferral prevents the stated verification closure
analysis: The safety plan records deferred HIL and says early-implementation credit cannot be earned until its conditions are met. Plans and host unit tests cannot replace target timing/fault-injection evidence.
action: Resource a controlled target bench and execute baseline-bound campaigns; if deferred, keep associated gate claims explicitly open.
closure: Target test logs, environment/calibration records, anomaly disposition and independent review.

title: Tool self-tests and classification do not complete qualification
analysis: In-house safety-relevant tools have open TQR records and review work; compiler/runner pinning is also open. Agreement between tools sharing assumptions does not authenticate the standard.
action: Complete TI/TD/TCL decisions and applicable qualification records; test error detection against independently sourced criteria and pin the toolchain.
closure: Reviewed use-case-specific tool qualification, known limitations, detection evidence and immutable versions.

title: Reuse/qualification conclusions remain unconfirmed
analysis: The work product requests review of RA-01…RA-09 and records for remaining safety-relevant components; initialized submodules establish access, not qualification.
action: Review component use cases, interfaces, failure modes and configuration; close reuse assessments and safety component evidence needs.
closure: Reviewed SCQ/RA records and traceable component qualification evidence for the actual use.

title: Confirmation-measure coverage and independence still require source verification
analysis: The plan itself questions whether several rows are required in the licensed edition. Planned I3 rigor does not validate the underlying table transcription.
action: Verify every measure, applicable ASIL and independence requirement directly against Part 2; reconcile the CR list and schedule.
closure: Source/page-referenced approved confirmation matrix with signed results at required gates.

title: Historical baseline statements can be mistaken for current status
analysis: WP-M-01 already identifies this as a historical starting point, but its old facts could be read as current status. Current assurance records and safety.yaml differ. This is a clarity observation, not proof of an incorrect historical assessment.
action: Mark historical observations and reconcile assessment baselines, software pins, current status and impact records without rewriting history.
closure: Baseline crosswalk plus reviewed current-status statements and supersession links.

title: Assessment template contains stale status/coordination references
analysis: WP-K-04 says the confirmation folder is to be created via OI-6, although the folder exists and WP-M-02 OI-5 reports closure; no FSA is actually executed.
action: Update template coordination links through normal document control, leaving execution/approval fields explicitly unperformed.
closure: Correct reference and folder state with reviewed revision; no fabricated assessor signature or result.

title: The current safety case does not support release
analysis: The work product explicitly disclaims a release claim; machine-readable records show 0 accepted claims, 0 accepted evidence and 41 open defeaters. Structural validity is not evidence sufficiency.
action: Close safety-critical defeaters with configuration-bound evidence; obtain applicable verification, confirmation and assessment before release.
closure: Accepted claim/evidence chains, dispositioned defeaters, FSA and signed release record.

title: Retrofit tailoring must cover residual production/supplier responsibilities
analysis: The strategy tails production to installation and distributed development to upstream reuse. These are proposed project arguments; supplier responsibilities and applicable obligations need source-based review.
action: Map each applicable Part 7/8 requirement to installer, upstream supplier or LionDriver; justify retained/allocated/tailored obligations.
closure: Approved obligation allocation, installation/process evidence and residual-risk disposition.

title: Proven-in-use non-use is a declared strategy, not a blanket compliance failure
analysis: The project deliberately makes no proven-in-use claim. Likewise, ASIL decomposition is not automatically mandatory. Requirement applicability needs an approved rationale.
action: Keep the alternative routes visible and justify non-use; do not count an unused route as complied with or mark it failed solely because no artifact exists.
closure: Source-verified applicability/tailoring decisions and no contradictory reuse/decomposition claims.
